chapter: Return to New Orleans and Preservation Hall
title: Returning to banjo at Preservation Hall under Punch Miller
summary: He went back to banjo because of the Hall, joined Punch Miller's Sunday night band later Sweet Emma's with the Humphreys.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: You said you would have never thought about playing banjo?
Yeah, when I was there in Florida and all over the month. Oh, when the Hall was there, yeah.

That's the only reason why I went back on banjo, you see. Yeah. And like I said, I enjoyed Luce Band, and when I came back, like I said before, I lost my scene now after so. So Punch had a Sunday night date there, and he requested for them to hire me. So I stayed with that band. When Punch died, and there was some other trumpet player, and that's why. Then they made it Sweet Emmons night, called it her band, Pussy and Willie Humphrey, came in there and started playing. Now they're the top band today, because Jaffa is the managing leader of that band, you see. So when I went to Chicago, I lost my scene out there. I went to the jazz, and that man called me to Wicker Mountain. And the fellow died. Well I was single, I wasn't married to this woman, and I was single, I had to stay up there. Until the place closed up. The man had me on notice for about two or three months. Every month he had to give me a notice, you know. He couldn't make up his mind. So my wife wouldn't come back. I said, no, we're going to stay here until he's given me, tell me, you've got to give me a four-witch or two-witch notice, you know. And we had a big place up there, man. She had come from California and I got married, honey, I got married up there. I'm my third husband, and she's my third wife.
Yeah. And so you played some at Preservation Hall before you went up to Chicago?
No, at Preservation Hall. And you said 60, I said 60.
Yeah, no, but I mean before you went to Chicago the second time. Oh, the second time, yeah.

Well, that's what I say, I lost my seniority. I went to work at the Red Guard, but I went to work for two nights. And those guys, they really didn't know anything about banjo, you had to play that. But I had, just like I say, coming up in my lifetime, I always learned songs, they come out, most of us just in my age, you see. Mm-hmm.
